title: Introduction to Web Development

setup.title: Web Development workstation setup
setup.description: A skippable, verified setup module outside the eight instructional weeks. Prepare VS Code and a modern browser, Git, and GitHub before Week 1.

capabilities.title: Visual Studio Code
capabilities.description: Visual Studio Code is reusable across every introductory course that requires it.
instructions: Install VS Code from the official Windows package.
Official download or account page: https://code.visualstudio.com/Download
verification: Open a course folder and create a file.

capabilities.title: Modern browser with DevTools
capabilities.description: Modern browser with DevTools is reusable across every introductory course that requires it.
instructions: Use an updated Edge, Chrome, or Firefox installation.
Official download or account page: https://www.microsoft.com/edge/download
verification: Open DevTools and inspect a local page.

capabilities.title: Git for Windows
capabilities.description: Git for Windows is reusable across every introductory course that requires it.
instructions: Install Git, keep the recommended beginner defaults, then configure your name and email.
Official download or account page: https://git-scm.com/download/win
verification: Run git --version, git config user.name, and git config user.email.

capabilities.title: GitHub account
capabilities.description: GitHub account is reusable across every introductory course that requires it.
instructions: Create or reuse a personal GitHub account and configure account recovery.
Official download or account page: https://github.com/signup
verification: Create a private practice repository, connect a local repository, and push one commit.

target.learner: A tertiary fresher with basic computer literacy and no assumed programming experience.
target.professionalOutcome: Recognize Web Development syntax, write and debug small programs, and complete beginner practical-exam tasks independently.
specialGoals: Publish a final repository with an honest README.

assumptions: Windows is the primary host operating system.
The separate setup module is completed or verified before Week 1.
Essential explanations are bundled for offline-first study.
Skill Checks allow unlimited attempts while preserving the two-failure recovery lock.

weeks.title: HTML Structure and the Browser
weeks.outcome: Build, debug, explain, and verify a semantic personal profile page.

study.objective: Learn and actively rehearse HTML element, attribute, document outline, link, validator so you can explain, select, debug, and apply them while creating a semantic personal profile page.

resources.purpose: Learn the exact definitions, applications, and mistakes assessed by the Week 1 Skill Check, then preview the a semantic personal profile page contract.
Rehearse the same five weekly concepts through prediction, error recognition, and explanation without affecting progression.

skillCheck.title: HTML Structure and the Browser Skill Check
skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 1 guide defines HTML element. Which description matches that definition?

options.label: a marked-up part of document structure

questions.explanation: HTML element means a marked-up part of document structure; it is used to use a heading element for the page heading. Avoid this mistake: choose tags only for visual appearance.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to use a heading element for the page heading. Which concept from the Week 1 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: HTML element is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to choose tags only for visual appearance.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for attribute, which warning identifies the error to avoid?

options.label: skip levels to obtain a smaller font
write click here without destination context
treat a rendered page as proof of valid structure

questions.explanation: attribute means extra element information; it is used to add href to a link. Avoid this mistake: place every value outside quotes.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to place every value outside quotes. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: attribute is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to place every value outside quotes.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 1 guide correctly demonstrates document outline?

options.label: follow h1 with section h2 headings
use a heading element for the page heading

questions.explanation: document outline means meaningful heading hierarchy; it is used to follow h1 with section h2 headings. Avoid this mistake: skip levels to obtain a smaller font.

questions.prompt: Which weekly concept is demonstrated by this guide activity: follow h1 with section h2 headings?
questions.explanation: document outline is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to skip levels to obtain a smaller font.

questions.prompt: A learner must explain link before coding. Which explanation is accurate?

options.label: a tool reporting markup conformance issues
a marked-up part of document structure

questions.explanation: link means navigation to another resource; it is used to use a meaningful anchor label. Avoid this mistake: write click here without destination context.

questions.prompt: The guide describes "navigation to another resource". Which term does it describe?
questions.explanation: link is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to write click here without destination context.

questions.prompt: Which mistake would show that validator was misunderstood?

options.label: choose tags only for visual appearance
skip levels to obtain a smaller font
treat a rendered page as proof of valid structure

questions.explanation: validator means a tool reporting markup conformance issues; it is used to repair an unclosed element. Avoid this mistake: treat a rendered page as proof of valid structure.

questions.prompt: To avoid this error—treat a rendered page as proof of valid structure—which weekly concept must the learner apply?
questions.explanation: validator is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to treat a rendered page as proof of valid structure.

builds.title: Microbuild: a semantic personal profile page
builds.outcome: A working, tested a semantic personal profile page.
builds.brief: Deliverable: a semantic personal profile page. Required behavior: demonstrate HTML element, attribute, document outline, link, validator; complete one normal, one boundary, and one invalid case; and keep a short expected-versus-actual test record. Evidence: the exact run command, the repaired defect, the three final results, and an honest README.

steps.text: Write a three-case contract for a semantic personal profile page: one normal case, one boundary case, and one invalid case. For each, record the input or action and the expected result before coding.
Create the runnable source and implement the normal case first. Make HTML element, attribute, document outline visible in the code or interface, then run the exact launch command once.

Add the boundary and invalid-case behavior using link and validator. Deliberately reproduce this weekly mistake—treat a rendered page as proof of valid structure—record the symptom, repair one cause, and rerun the same case.
Run all three contract cases again. In README, record the environment, exact run command, expected versus actual results, repaired defect, and one known limit.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A learner can follow the README command and run a semantic personal profile page through its stated normal case without an unexplained error.
The finished work visibly demonstrates the Week 1 concepts: HTML element, attribute, document outline, link, validator.
The test record lists normal, boundary, and invalid inputs or actions with both expected and actual results.
The debugging note names the failing case, observed symptom, root cause, single repair, successful rerun, and one known limit.

hints: If the normal case fails, reduce it to the smallest input or action involving HTML element and inspect the observed value before editing.
If the boundary or invalid case fails, revisit the guide warning "treat a rendered page as proof of valid structure" and change one cause at a time.

Rehearse the same five weekly concepts through prediction, error recognition, and explanation without affecting progression.

skillCheck.title: CSS Foundations Skill Check
skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 2 guide defines selector. Which description matches that definition?
questions.explanation: selector means a pattern choosing elements; it is used to target .card. Avoid this mistake: use an id for every repeated component.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to target .card. Which concept from the Week 2 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: selector is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use an id for every repeated component.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for cascade, which warning identifies the error to avoid?

options.label: use margin when the background should include the space
expect an undefined variable to choose any color
use low opacity for essential labels

questions.explanation: cascade means rules deciding which declaration wins; it is used to compare specificity and source order. Avoid this mistake: add !important before finding the cause.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to add !important before finding the cause. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: cascade is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to add !important before finding the cause.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 2 guide correctly demonstrates box model?
questions.explanation: box model means content, padding, border, and margin; it is used to add inner space with padding. Avoid this mistake: use margin when the background should include the space.

questions.prompt: Which weekly concept is demonstrated by this guide activity: add inner space with padding?
questions.explanation: box model is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use margin when the background should include the space.

questions.prompt: A learner must explain custom property before coding. Which explanation is accurate?
questions.explanation: custom property means a reusable CSS value; it is used to define --color-accent. Avoid this mistake: expect an undefined variable to choose any color.

questions.prompt: The guide describes "a reusable CSS value". Which term does it describe?
questions.explanation: custom property is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to expect an undefined variable to choose any color.

questions.prompt: Which mistake would show that contrast was misunderstood?

options.label: use an id for every repeated component
use low opacity for essential labels
use margin when the background should include the space

questions.explanation: contrast means visual difference supporting readability; it is used to check text against its background. Avoid this mistake: use low opacity for essential labels.

questions.prompt: To avoid this error—use low opacity for essential labels—which weekly concept must the learner apply?
questions.explanation: contrast is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use low opacity for essential labels.

weeks.outcome: Build, debug, explain, and verify a mobile-first responsive information page.

study.objective: Learn and actively rehearse viewport, media query, flexbox, grid, mobile first so you can explain, select, debug, and apply them while creating a mobile-first responsive information page.

resources.purpose: Learn the exact definitions, applications, and mistakes assessed by the Week 3 Skill Check, then preview the a mobile-first responsive information page contract.
Rehearse the same five weekly concepts through prediction, error recognition, and explanation without affecting progression.

skillCheck.title: Responsive Layout Skill Check
skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 3 guide defines viewport. Which description matches that definition?
questions.explanation: viewport means the visible browser area; it is used to include the viewport meta tag. Avoid this mistake: assume desktop width on phones.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to include the viewport meta tag. Which concept from the Week 3 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: viewport is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to assume desktop width on phones.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for media query, which warning identifies the error to avoid?

options.label: create device-specific breakpoints for every model
use absolute positioning for normal flow
force every grid to fixed pixel columns
hide core content on small screens

questions.explanation: media query means conditional CSS based on environment; it is used to enhance layout above a breakpoint. Avoid this mistake: create device-specific breakpoints for every model.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to create device-specific breakpoints for every model. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: media query is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to create device-specific breakpoints for every model.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 3 guide correctly demonstrates flexbox?
questions.explanation: flexbox means one-dimensional layout; it is used to align a navigation row. Avoid this mistake: use absolute positioning for normal flow.

questions.prompt: Which weekly concept is demonstrated by this guide activity: align a navigation row?
questions.explanation: flexbox is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to use absolute positioning for normal flow.

questions.prompt: A learner must explain grid before coding. Which explanation is accurate?

options.label: base styles for narrow screens then enhancement

questions.explanation: grid means two-dimensional track layout; it is used to create responsive cards. Avoid this mistake: force every grid to fixed pixel columns.

questions.prompt: The guide describes "two-dimensional track layout". Which term does it describe?
questions.explanation: grid is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to force every grid to fixed pixel columns.

questions.prompt: Which mistake would show that mobile first was misunderstood?

options.label: hide core content on small screens
create device-specific breakpoints for every model
use absolute positioning for normal flow

questions.explanation: mobile first means base styles for narrow screens then enhancement; it is used to add min-width queries. Avoid this mistake: hide core content on small screens.

questions.prompt: To avoid this error—hide core content on small screens—which weekly concept must the learner apply?
questions.explanation: mobile first is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to hide core content on small screens.

questions.prompt: The Week 4 guide defines DOM. Which description matches that definition?

options.label: a reported interaction or lifecycle occurrence
changing input text into a number
the object model of the loaded document

questions.explanation: DOM means the object model of the loaded document; it is used to select a result element. Avoid this mistake: treat HTML source and live DOM as always identical.

learnerGuide.finishedResult: A runnable an accessible responsive interactive site deployed with GitHub Pages, a three-case expected-versus-actual test record, a specific debugging note, and reproducible README instructions.

conceptRefs.relevance: The build applies relative URL in a visible program decision.

proof.prompt: Prove that an accessible responsive interactive site deployed with GitHub Pages can be reproduced, survives the three required cases, and includes one evidence-backed repair.

evidence.label: Public or private GitHub repository URL containing source and README
Exact run command, three expected-versus-actual results, and repaired defect

What will you test first when a similar program fails again?
